title: Treasury liquidity-support buyback operation (TIPS 10-30Y, $500M cap, 1:40pm ET)
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Buyback Operations (August 2026 refunding, masthead 'For Publication August 5, 2026'), PDF text layer decompressed direct 2026-09-08 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 125,547 bytes, md5 79b65955e74a59f6bebff3adf8ba7b35 — byte-identical to the 09-03/09-05/09-06/09-08 fetches recorded on treasury-buyback-increase-2026-09-09) — the row reads verbatim announce 9/14/2026, operation 9/15/2026 1:40 pm - 2:00 pm, settle 9/16/2026, Liquidity Support, TIPS 10Y to 30Y, maturity range 09/16/2036 - 09/15/2056, min $0, max $500 million. Stays estimate on the same two counts as its nominal siblings (treasury-buyback-10y20y-2026-09-10, treasury-buyback-20y30y-2026-09-24, treasury-buyback-10y20y-2026-11-04, all estimate off this same document): a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and the confirming primary is the 09-14 operation announcement rather than this document. Re-verified at the primary 2026-09-08
notes: PROMOTED to canonical 2026-09-08 by this event's own initial research, from the single proposal that existed for this id (proposals/treasury-buyback-tips-10y30y-2026-09-15.from-treasury-buyback-increase-2026-09-09.json, filed the same day by the 09-09 buyback-increase D-1 sweep). Ledger: docs/research/events/treasury-buyback-tips-10y30y-2026-09-15.md. The proposer's read is upheld and sharpened on three primary-verified counts. (1) sb0607 (fetched direct 2026-09-08, HTTP 200, full body read) does NOT cover this operation: its title is 'Nominal Long-End Liquidity Support Buybacks' and its body names 'longer-dated nominal coupon securities (the 10-year to 20-year sector and the 20-year to 30-year sector)' only. The $500M cap here is untouched, so this is the doubled window's control. (2) The cap has never been the binding constraint, but the proposer's 'never came close' understates WHY: across all four operations under the current 10Y-30Y label (2025-11-12, 2025-12-23, 2026-03-25, 2026-05-28) offers EXCEEDED the $500M cap every time (1.5x-2.8x) and Treasury still accepted only $142M/$108M/$110M/$91M, an 18.2-28.4% fill and a 9.1-14.5% hit rate on par offered. Treasury is rationing on PRICE, not running out of sellers — the exact inverse of the nominal long end, where the cap bound 25/25 and 24/26. (3) The label is a maturity range, not a sector: every eligible line in all four operations (15-16 lines, buybacks_security_details, fetched 2026-09-08) is a Feb-15 maturity between 2040 and 2055 — the 30-year TIPS strip, zero 10-year TIPS lines, because the window opens one day after the newest 10Y TIPS matures. Two further facts this research adds: 110 days will have elapsed since the last long-TIPS operation (2026-05-28), the longest gap in the series since it began 2024-04-17; and this is the ONLY TIPS 10Y-30Y operation on the entire August-2026 refunding schedule (the other two TIPS rows, 9/29 and 10/21, are the 1Y-10Y bucket at $750M, proposed here). Low impact is honest about size — $500M against $8.0B of 30Y TIPS issued on 2026-08-20 alone is a 16:1 issuance-to-cap ratio — not about analytical value: this is the one operation in the 09-10 to 09-24 corridor that touches the instrument the long-end selloff is actually happening in. Estimate-labeled; nothing here licenses an entry.
